segments.t: Hotel manager Mikhail Jekovich knocks on the room door because guests are complaining about the noise. When Mikhail keeps poking around, Senya knocks him out with another vase, and Chef Barinov forbids any more violence.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'The hotel guests are complaining about loud noise.' Adding that the hotel guests are complaining about loud noise fills in the missing piece for Barinov.
'And what are you doing here?' With the hotel and room hanging in the air, Mikhail puts Barinov on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'I brought a dish from the chef.' Since he brought a dish, Fedya does not waste words on excuses.
'And who is mooing loudly in there?' Asking who mooing loudly in there is is how Mikhail puts Barinov on the spot.

'That is just from great pleasure.' Saying that that is just from great pleasure is how Fedya sets the tone with Barinov. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'That is it, go away from here quickly.' Because that is it go away from here quickly, Mikhail treats the matter as settled.
'It seems we did not get caught here.' Explaining that it seems they did not get caught here lays the cards on the table for Barinov.

'Why do you poke your nose everywhere?' Wondering why Fedya poke Fedya's nose everywhere is how Barinov puts Fedya on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.

'We need to decide something, Chef.' Here needing to decide something sets up the next turn in their exchange. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front.
'We are already running out of vases.' Pointing out that they are already running out of vases gives Barinov a sobering reality check.
'He hanged himself out of jealousy.' Over the hotel and the plan, Fedya answers Barinov without a second thought.

'Nobody is going to die here today!' Saying that nobody is going to die here today is how Barinov takes charge of the moment. Russian stacks "never" or "nothing" together with "not", doubling the refusal for extra weight. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Before Chef Barinov can figure out how to untangle this mess, Kostya arrives at the door with a bottle of champagne. See you next time!
